activity_text: Anti-Gram+, Antiviral, Spermicidal, Anti-HIV, Hemolytic, Anticancer
comments_text: Discovery: Isolated in 1939. The major form in the natural mixture (80% of the total gramicidins A, B, and C). Soluble in the lower alcohols, acetic acid, and pyridine; almost insoluble in water due to its hydrophobic nature. Chemical modification: Synthesized non-ribosomally by a multienzyme complex. Both the N- and C-termini are chemically modified (CHO formylated at the N-terminus and NHCH2CH2OH at the C-terminus). N-terminus is rich in Val, while the C-terminus is rich in Trp. Amino acids 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12 are D-amino acids. Structure in lipid bilayer: It forms a special helical structure followed by head-to-head dimerization into a cation channel in lipid bilayer with the C-terminus exposed (Ketchem RR et al 1996 J Biomol NMR 8: 1). You can rotate, zoom, and view the 3D structure here in the PDB. Structures solved in organic solvents by x-ray diffraction are believed to be non-channel forms. Activity: active against Gram+ B. subtilis ATCC 663 (MIC 2.5 uM), S. aureus ATCC 6538 (MIC 2.5 uM), S. pyogenes ATCC 1961 (MIC 0.16 uM) but not E.coli BL21 ( Wang et al., 2012). ALso active against D. pneumoniae Type I (MBC 2 ug/ml), S. hemolyticus group A type 6 (MBC 2 ug/ml), and S. aureus (MBC 10 ug/ml), minimall bactericidal concentration based on no growth on blood agar. This peptide shows effects on HIV and HSV infections (Life Sci. 1994;54(1):PL5-9.; Arch Virol 1997; 142: 2225-35). gA also has anticancer effect. MOA:bacteria: it forms a ion channel in membranes. permeated bacterial membranes. Hydroxyl radical formation is reproted to play a role as well in the case of S. aureus ( Liou et al., 2015). In vitro toxicity: human RBC: HC50 5 uM, highly hemolytic. MOA:cancer: It downregulates EGR4 expression, inhibits cholangiocarcinoma cell growth through EGR4 (early growth response protein 4), and induces necroptotic cell death ( Gong et al., 2020). AMPs in use: it is the first peptide antibiotic commercially made and used clinically for topical treatment of infected wounds, eye, nose, throat infections. It is not suitable for systemic use due to high hemolytic toxicity. Other forms: Gramicidin D is a mixture of 80% gramicidin A, 5% B, and 15% C. Updated 2/2012; Jan2018; 6/2019; Jan2020; 7/2020; formatted 5/2024; updated 8/2025.
title: STUDIES ON A BACTERICIDAL AGENT EXTRACTED FROM A SOIL BACILLUS: III. PREPARATION AND ACTIVITY OF A PROTEIN-FREE FRACTION.
